decisions.decision: Use a committed observations file instead of writing a temporary file in tests
decisions.rationale: Two test binaries running concurrently wrote to the same temporary file path, causing race conditions where one truncated the file while the other read it. Using a committed fixture eliminates the race condition and allows the residuals to be checked by eye.
decisions.quote: The repair is that the observations are now a **committed** file,

decisions.decision: Include the ephemeris residuals command in the documentation's worked examples
decisions.rationale: The new committed observations fixture serves as a demonstrable example that can be generated into the manual alongside other CLI examples.
decisions.quote: 37 worked examples now, because the fixture is a demonstrable example

prerequisites.text: The observations file parser skips blank lines and lines starting with hash characters.
prerequisites.quote: Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped.

alternatives.alternative: Writing the observations fixture dynamically to a temporary directory during test runs
alternatives.reason: Concurrent test binaries writing to the same temporary path raced, resulting in truncated reads and flaky test failures.
alternatives.quote: The repair is that the observations are a committed file rather than one a test invents

consequences.text: The test fixture cannot race when test binaries run concurrently.
Residuals are known in advance and can be checked by eye.
consequences.quote: so the residuals are known in advance and can be checked by eye.

consequences.text: The fixture is generated into the manual alongside the rest of the worked examples.
consequences.quote: the fixture is a demonstrable example and is generated into the manual alongside the rest.
